leverage.exposure: A leveraged position is open and must be closed before the matchday locks, or the entire matchday scores zero. That is the one risk that outranks everything else here. The mitigating fact is time: the lock is nearly a week away, so the deficit costs nothing today and should not be used as a reason to kill a good buy — only whether a position can be unwound by the lock constrains it. The recommended sale clears the hole outright and leaves genuine room on top. Flips would deepen the leverage before they resolve it, which is why they are sequenced after the sale and capped by spending power rather than by cash; taken in the ranked order only the top few fit, and each unwinds by instant sale to the board at market value well inside the deadline. Every flip must still leave at least eleven players and a non-negative balance at the lock.

binding_gap: The binding gap is not a position, it is the deficit, and the shape of the squad is what makes it binding. Only one sale can be made before the eleven becomes unfillable, so that one sale has to cover the whole hole by itself. Guirassy is the only player who both clears it and is not currently contributing. After he goes the squad sits at eleven with a single striker and exactly one legal formation, which is safe but has no slack — the next gap to fill is a second striker, and the board has nothing worth buying there.
